messages:
sam: Quick run summary: brought up a 7B model with MQA int8 quant, compared PCIe vs SXM intra-node topologies. Focus: KV cache behavior, NUMA pinning, NVLink routing, and kernel differences. posting configs + a few charts.
maya: Nice — what's the workload (batch, seq len, steady-state vs cold)?
sam: batch=8, seq=1024, steady-state (after kv warmup). measuring p50/p95/p99 lat and tok/s. ran on eu-west (SXM) and us-west (PCIe) clusters, and a simulated PCIe-only mode on SXM box by disabling NVLink.
kevin: Can you paste the run command? curious about flags
sam: ```
./bench_run.sh \
  --model redwood-7b-mqa \
  --devices 4 \
  --batch 8 \
  --seq 1024 \
  --kv-cache on \
  --quant int8 \
  --pin numa \
  --disable-nvlink false \
  --kernel auto
```
anita: Top-level takeaways? tl;dr please :)
sam: TL;DR — SXM with NVLink wins tail latency and variance: ~25% lower p99 vs PCIe on same model+quant. PCIe nodes showed ~10% higher avg latency but are cheaper per-node. NUMA pinning reduced latency jitter on PCIe setups by ~12–18% (less effect on SXM when NVLink enabled). Kernel choice mattered for int8: using fused-attn kernels + custom matmul path gave ~7% latency drop on SXM.
lucas: Charts?
sam: Uploaded; (internal) https://s3.redwood-internal/bench/1818234000/latency_p99.png and throughput_chart.png and kernel_compare.png — summary notes below.
kevin: Did you run a PCIe-emulation on SXM (nvlink off) and real PCIe? curious if topology or driver is the main cause.
sam: Yup. Two experiments: (A) real PCIe machines (A100-pcie) and (B) SXM with NVLink disabled via BIOS/driver to remove fabric benefits. Emulated PCIe on SXM performed slightly better than real PCIe — suggests driver/kernel + packing differences also play a role. infra-bot flagged driver versions.
infra-bot: NOTICE: us-west PCIe fleet currently on driver 510.x; eu-west SXM fleet running 545.x. Driver/kernel differences may affect cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel selection. :information_source:
maya: Any quality regressions from int8 quant+qat?
sam: Minimal. Eval on our holdout: ROUGE-L drop ~0.4–0.6 absolute on long-context generation, perplexity delta small. We ran calibration with 2k in-domain prompts. Full eval notebook: https://notebooks.internal/reports/1818234000
anita: Recommendations for prod rollouts?
kevin: Propose: 1) autodetect topology (NVLink rings, NUMA map) at agent startup and expose a --topology-mode flag. 2) Default to NUMA pinning for PCIe nodes. 3) Select optimized kernel path for SXM when detected. 4) Add fallback to lower-quant model variant if p99 exceeds SLO.
sam: I'll draft a PR with a small topology detector script + recommended launch config. Snippet:
```
# detect nvlink presence
lspci | grep -i "nvidia"
# parse nvlink links
nvidia-smi topo -m
# set envs
export NUMA_CPUS=0-31
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
```
lucas: Also include cost-per-token estimates in the PR for capacity sizing. SXM throughput ~1.25x but node cost ~1.35x => per-token cost ~1.1x. PCIe throughput ~0.9x but node cost ~0.8x => per-token cost ~0.72x of SXM in raw infra cost, YMMV with packing.
maya: Are there specific kernel flags we should toggle for int8? I saw mention of fused-attn.
sam: Fused-attn + custom int8 GEMM path (our patched cublasLt kernels) gave best tail on SXM. On PCIe older driver falls back to non-fused path. We should gate the kernel with a health-check microbenchmark at startup.
kevin: Good call. Also add a small eval to ensure quantization quality per-model before enabling in hosted traffic. automation should block if ROUGE drop > 1.0.
anita: Nice work. Next steps: PR for config + detector, cost appendix, and a short runbook for oncall describing when to fallback to larger model. :thumbsup:
sam: Will open PR today and ping y'all. attaching raw logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-19T14:12:01Z] p50=32ms p95=120ms p99=210ms tok/s=14500 (SXM NVLink fused)
[2026-03-19T14:12:01Z] p50=40ms p95=140ms p99=265ms tok/s=11600 (PCIe)
```
lucas: Thanks — please include driver/kernel matrix in PR so infra can schedule upgrades where it helps most.
maya: SG, ping me when PR is up and I'll review the eval notebooks.
sam: will do — thanks! :rocket:
